body:
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced that the central bank will reduce the number of rate-setting meetings starting in 2027, noting that while eight meetings per year is “the right number” for the FOMC, one of them will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy starting in 2027. The remainder will be policy-setting meetings.

In 2028, the Fed will plan to host two meetings focused on strategy discussions and the remaining six will be centered on policy setting, Warsh said. [...] Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said the central bank will cut back on the number of meetings where members vote on rates. [...] Said Warsh: “We believe eight meetings per year is the right number for the FOMC, but in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated. The rest will be regular FOMC policy setting meetings, and I expect that in 2028 we’ll have two meetings dedicated discussions of strategy and six for setting policy.”
